text: What shall you see in the Shulamite? She comes as a company of the camps. How you do beautify your footsteps in sandals, O daughter of Nabad. The proportions of your thighs are likened to pendants -- works of the hands of a craftsman.
Your navel is as; [[2]basin [1]a turned], not lacking mixed wine. Your belly is as a heap of grain shut up in lilies.
[[2]two [3]breasts [1]Your] are as two fawns, twins of the doe.
Your neck is as a tower of ivory; ; your eyes are as lakes in Heshbon, by the gates of the daughter of many. Your nose is as the tower ; of Lebanon, watching in front of Damascus.
Your head upon you is as Carmel, and the braid of your head is as purple, with the king being bound by its passing by.
How beautiful and how delicious, O love, in your luxuries.
This your greatness is likened to the palm, and ; your breasts to the clusters of grapes.
I said, I will ascend unto the palm, I will seize ; its heights; and [[2]shall indeed be [1]your breasts] as clusters of grapes of the grapevine, and the scent of your nose as apples.
And your throat is as [[2]wine ; [1]good], going to; my beloved man; in straightness, suiting in my lips and teeth.
I turn to my beloved man, and [[2]is towards [3]me ; [1]his turning].
Come, O my beloved man! we should go forth into the field; we should lodge in towns.

We should rise early to the vineyards; we should see if [[3]bloomed [1]the [2]grapevine]; if [[2]bloomed ; [1]the blossoms]; if [[3]bloomed [1]the [2]pomegranates]. There I will give ; my breasts to you.
The mandrakes gave a scent, and at our doors are all the fruit trees -- new to old. O my beloved man, I kept them for you.
